question: Do anonymous numerical representations agree on repeatable changes in around-ear EEG, beyond phase-randomized controls, and does frozen detection transfer to unused source participants and a different dataset?
freeze_stage: After technical source inventory; before expanded waveform feature extraction. Eight source participants were explored in Experiments 001/002 and are explicitly flagged in the corpus protocol.
input: All qualified recordings in corpus-manifest-v1.json. Numeric discovery functions receive samples in microvolts, sample rate and validity only. Dataset/participant/session/channel names and task labels stay in the curator/evaluation layer.
continuity: Split at every logged boundary and remove BAD intervals. Never join context across gaps. Drop feature windows outside a native continuous interval. Feature timestamps remain in native recording seconds.
channel_selection: EEG channels only; exclude channels explicitly marked bad in source technical metadata. Retain unknown status with disclosure. Require at least two channels.
interpretation: These are distinct numerical representations, not independently pretrained LLMs reading raw EEG. None is assumption-free. A representation-level change is not a proven mental or clinical state change.

fit.sampling: Evenly spaced eligible rows, equal maximum contribution per recording
fit.reference: Coordinatewise training median and robust scale

controls.selection: First continuous interval at least 144 seconds; use 12-second halos around a 120-second central interval. Selection uses continuity and length only, not observed signal values.
controls.rules: Same original segments and frozen reference/thresholds. Publish validity and exposure for each variant. Independent phase preserves per-channel Fourier magnitudes; shared phase additionally preserves cross-spectra. Surrogates change temporal localization, so their event counts alone are not a biological null proof.

aggregation: Participant-recording is the statistical unit, not an overlapping window. Publish each record; aggregate medians with participant bootstrap intervals (1000 replicates, seed 17) only where at least two records exist. Both datasets currently have one record per source participant.
evaluation: Internal test and external results are descriptive frozen evaluations; external prior-exposed and prior-unexposed records reported separately. No clinical accuracy, token semantics, universal geometry or cross-device equivalence claim follows from agreement alone.
failure_policy: Preserve every source record in the coverage table, with failed/quarantined or insufficient-context reasons. Do not tune to external observations. Corrections that alter a result require a new recorded run and public correction note.
